answer_1.quote: We fine‑tune summarization models with different capacities, and use them to produce a diverse set of model‑generated summaries of CNN/DM articles, which we label for consistency using a 540B LLM.
answer_1.outputs: model‑generated summaries together with factual consistency labels

answer_2.quote: We evaluate models using ROC‑AUC in a binary classification setting, and we also report ROUGE scores for summarization model training as well as extractive fragment coverage and density as abstractiveness metrics.

answer_3.quote: We first train a diverse collection of summarization models … The resulting document‑summary pairs are then annotated by prompting a LLM to predict the corresponding factual consistency label.
methods: zero‑shot prompting for binary consistency labeling

answer_4.quote: We perform human evaluation carried out by domain experts. We evaluate 100 examples from our dataset, using binary judgements based on the attribution definition from Rashkin et al.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators provide binary judgments (consistent/inconsistent) based on whether all information in the summary is fully attributable to the source document.
